text: A creased white swim-team tryout poster shows a swimmer in a black cap and goggles, one arm bent high above splashes of blue water. Green lettering tops the sheet. Below the swimmer, red Otter Power text leads into large orange letters with dark blue shadows asking Can You Swim to Success?

Two cartoon germs stand in the center of a pale, creased flu-shot poster. The front germ is orange-brown, the rear one green; both have spiky round bodies, thin limbs and black burglar-style eye masks. Bold rounded black lettering sits above and below them, with Get Immunized Today! across the bottom.

A cream-colored Blackwell Academy girls' dormitory map uses thick black outlines around white rooms and gray corridors. The floor plan bends upward at the left. Mint-green name labels mark eight numbered rooms along the lower wing, with bathrooms near the middle and a TV lounge, stairs and vending area at the right.

Three notices overlap. A large grayscale HIV and AIDS awareness poster has sweeping abstract shapes and red pins at its upper corners. Beneath it, a narrow handwritten reward notice has a red, double-underlined heading. A torn horizontal note at lower right uses slanting black capitals and emphatic underlining to complain about stolen face cream.

A slightly crumpled white sheet has fine blue ruling and a thin blue border. Bold, rounded black handwriting fills nearly the whole page beneath the heading 'Don't Let Big Brother Watch You.' Widely spaced paragraphs lead down to a centered meeting date and location. There are no illustrations.

A red outlined warning triangle with a black exclamation mark tops a white campus-safety notice. The large heading 'Be Alert on Campus' is underlined. Three widely spaced safety tips in flowing black lettering occupy the middle, followed by an underlined web address near the bottom. Pale brown smudges mark the paper.

A large 'Geek Grrls Book Club' flyer overlaps a smaller bicycle-for-sale notice. The club flyer has a tan banner, brown type and a tall, uneven stack of multicolored books topped by an open book and turquoise glasses. At left, the sale notice shows a dark bicycle with yellow wheel reflectors against a brick wall.

A square cream-and-black poster reads 'The Vortex Club' in chunky, staggered lettering. A broad black spiral fills the lower two-thirds, its thick bands curling toward a small central opening. A bordered 'Coming Soon' label sits over the spiral near the bottom. The paper has worn brown edges.

A dark teal depression-support poster overlaps two small handwritten notices. White lettering surrounds a shadowy close-up of a face with a hand pressed to its forehead; the hotline number is heavily underlined. The lower-left notice asks for a statistics tutor and circles an A in red. The lower-right notice has a large red 'Lost Phone' heading.

A tall white vegan-club flyer tilts slightly to the left. Red outlined capitals at the top read 'Meat Is Still Murder.' Below black club lettering, a smiling green cartoon vegetable has large round eyes and a curved, elongated body. Loose black handwriting fills the lower half with meeting details.

A narrow, creased white flyer is topped by a roughly drawn black bat with spread wings. Tall black handwriting announces a 'Girls Nite Out' Halloween gathering, with 'Nightmare Before Christmas' centered in heavier capitals. Event details descend toward a playful winking face at the bottom. Small brown worn patches interrupt the edges.

A spotted brown deer faces the viewer between tall forest trunks, its ears raised. Broad, flat patches of green, blue and brown give the woodland picture a painted look. Long yellow shafts of sunlight cross the dark ground diagonally. Pale structures appear beyond the trees, and glossy glare washes across the lower right.

A black environmental poster shows a blue-and-green globe balanced above an outstretched hand. White slogans frame the illustration, with 'Save the Earth!' in large green capitals below. A small yellow picture taped over the lower-right area depicts a dark-haired figure with bare shoulders and hands held over their chest.
Dark trees arch over a clearing. Spindly white letters spell out Ghoul Days above an invitation to a Halloween costume dance at Prescott Gymnasium.

A white flyer has a red handwritten slogan above an underlined blue 'Young Guns Training' heading. Rounded black text is arranged in spacious centered blocks. A thin rectangular box encloses the hours and address near the bottom, with a discount line below. Faint tan stains dot the otherwise plain sheet.

A muted gray-and-brown 'Safe Not Sorry' poster shows two people embracing closely, one resting a hand on the other's brown hair. Large magenta graffiti across the lower half reads 'see Kate's video for proof.' A yellow handwritten quiet-hours notice peeks from behind its lower-left edge, held with beige tape.

A creased poster reads 'Don't Be a Zombie' in oversized dark red letters. Two stylized, bloodied zombie figures stare at handheld screens: one stands hunched above, while the other sits with legs stretched out amid dark red smears. Blue, black and white slogan lettering runs across the bottom, with one line inside a blue-gray band.

Dana Ward's profile has a pink background and a banner of friends standing shoulder to shoulder. Below her relationship status, two overlapping black-and-white portraits sit beside a grid of party photos.

A blue-topped mail window shows Dana Ward's sent Ghoul Days Halloween Party invitation. Her pink profile picture sits above several paragraphs, with a single message highlighted in the narrow column to the left.
A costume shop's website shows women in red and black corset dresses against a burgundy banner. A narrow list of categories runs down the left, with a sale strip below the article.
A crumpled sheet bears an apology to Dana in blue cursive. Words are crossed out. A separate offer of money sits near the bottom, above Logan's signature. Torn scraps stick out behind it.
A folded abstinence flyer shows two people leaning close together. Safe Not Sorry stretches across the top in purple and black. You Have a Choice covers the lower half in heavy black letters.
A letter to Katie rests on an open envelope. An ornate gray border and a small cross surround a few lines of formal cursive. The signature sits apart at lower right.
A cream slip lies across the lower left page of an open, red-bound Bible. Several lines beneath Matthew 11:28 are highlighted yellow. A sliver of blue paper peeks out on the opposite side.
A blue slip marked Proverbs 21:15 covers the upper right page of the Bible. Heavy pen strokes cross through the verse. The edge of the cream note is still visible on the left.
In a colorful cartoon, children gather under green leaves. An armored figure in a red cape holds a sword in front of them. Off to the side, another figure sits on the ground beside a bag.
Black ink skulls cluster in a hollow beneath a dark, gnarled tree. Long streaks run down from empty eye sockets. Smaller bones lie scattered across the white paper.
Five family members pose in two rows against dark wood paneling. A man in glasses and a tie stands behind three girls, beside a woman in white. Framed family pictures hang behind them.
Three lit orange pillar candles stand against a dark background. The shortest sits in front of the two taller ones, with wax running down their sides.
On the back of a postcard, a handwritten Bible verse and a message to Katie end with an underlined Pop. Two candles are sketched at lower left. A yellow stamp sits above Kate's Blackwell address.
Three students crowd into a glossy photo. The student at left wears rectangular glasses and pink. Purple streaks frame the middle student's face. Kate leans closest to the camera on the right.
A black tablet displays an email from Mom. The message fills a white panel on the right, with three inbox entries to the left and a purple strip of icons down the edge.

Three girls pose outdoors. Kate wears a dark cardigan over white, with a gold cross at her neck. One girl leans in from the left. Behind them, a girl in glasses and a pink headband holds an ice cream cone.
A box of Mystic Enchantment Cards has a black cover with cream lettering. Golden and brown fantasy figures crowd the front, lit by a diagonal flash of yellow and a small blue glow.
A science website leads with Join the Chrononauts. Dense paragraphs fill the middle column, flanked by a list of links and small pictures of galaxies and planets.
A blue spiral marks the black Wormhole website banner. Below an introduction, a colored grid bends into two funnel shapes. Small space photos line the right margin.
A petition asks why quantum physicists are trying to control time. A glowing blue hourglass illustrates the article. A column of empty sign-up fields ends in a red button on the left.
Max's purple-topped inbox is open to Too Much Time from Warren Graham. A small blue grid serves as his avatar. A long list of movie titles and comments fills the message.
Dana Ward's Ghoul Days Halloween Party invitation fills Max's inbox. Dana's pink avatar sits below the purple toolbar. The message ends with her signature as Dana of the Dead.
Max's profile shows her brown-bobbed portrait below a blue banner. Two doctored posts sit side by side: Max's head on a sheep, and on a monkey beside another monkey.
A cutout of Max's head is taped over a dark picture beside an animal skull. White scratches slash across both her eyes. Two strips of yellow tape stand out against the gray collage.
Yellow sticky notes overlap white scraps covered in handwriting. Time-travel questions and underlined phrases sit among sketches of clocks, a tornado and diagrams linked by arrows.

A young woman with a short brown bob stands beside a taller, bearded man in a brown plaid shirt. She wears a pink top marked 'Seattle'; both face the camera against a blue sky and city buildings. Curved edges and bright streaks of glare give the photograph a glossy, slightly bent appearance.

A smiling, freckled girl with a brown bob and visible braces poses in stadium seating above an ice hockey rink. Her oversized red jersey bears a large outlined S and a striped V-neck. Small players appear on the bright ice behind her, while glossy glare streaks across the photograph's lower right.

Three people pose on a huge gray sculpture of a shaggy, long-nosed figure with massive hands. One crouches at lower left; two perch beside its face at right, one standing in purple and red, the other sitting cross-legged. Chalk hearts and scribbles cover parts of the sculpture. Creases and glare cross the photograph.

A grayscale head-and-shoulders portrait depicts a man with swept-back dark hair, heavy eyebrows, a mustache, and a short beard. He looks directly outward with a neutral expression, wearing an open-collared pale shirt. Broad, angular patches of gray model his face against an almost white background.
A creased school schedule lays out the week in five columns. English AP is crossed out in purple on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday, with a little smiley face beside Tuesday's entry.
A white-bordered instant photo shows Victoria leaning toward the camera with her lips pressed together. White paint speckles her face and dark sweater above a patterned collar.
A child's watch has a bright blue strap and a green frog face with bulging eyes near the buckle end. Another frog sits behind the hands on the round dial.

A worn black-and-white missing-person flyer has a huge Missing heading across the top. At upper left, a portrait shows a young woman with straight, side-parted hair, a long dangling earring and a slight smile. The name Rachel Amber appears beneath. Bold information blocks fill the right and bottom within a thin black border.
Glossy gray-toned photos overlap. In front, a figure in a white top and dark boots sits leaning forward. The picture behind shows a similar figure facing the camera with hands held low.
A creased front page of The Independent carries the headline Weather Service Baffled by Snow. White flakes dot a dark street photograph. Narrow columns fill the space beneath it.
A blue poster shows two pale whales swimming under the large yellow words Save Our Bay. A smaller white slogan about the man-made drought sits at lower right.

A Two Whales fishing awards sign shares the wall with three glossy snapshots. In each, anglers hold a fish horizontally for the camera. The sturgeon stretches across two people. Handwritten labels identify each catch.
A Sasquatch field trip flyer resembles wooden signs hung between forest trees. A red circle marks a tiny dark shape among the trunks, with a circular enlargement beside it.
A blue sea-adventure flyer pairs a round portrait of a bearded captain in a knit cap with a white cabin boat. A yellow banner across the sky invites readers to join the Cousteaus.
A yellow-bordered Moby Deck Tours flyer centers a white passenger boat on blue water. Two small pictures beneath it show a sunset and a wooded shore.
A single silver key with a black plastic head shares a ring with a little black-and-white panda. The panda hangs with its arms out and a white patch on its belly.
A white cigarette pack with blue lettering lies open. Seven orange filters show at the open end, one cigarette protruding above the others.
Ten coins lie scattered. There are three quarters, one nickel and six copper pennies. Two of the pennies overlap near the lower left.
A yellow parking warning has red handwritten entries for September 21, 10:34 AM, and the plate TWNPKS. A red check marks Out of Parking Bay.
A cream Two Whales menu has a red border and a faint regional map behind the prices. A plate of eggs, toast and bacon illustrates the breakfast list. A blue whale swims along the bottom.
A creased front page of The Independent carries the headline Weather Service Baffled by Snow. White flakes dot a dark street photograph. Narrow columns fill the space beneath it.
In a signed color photo, a man in a light cap and red jacket has an arm around Joyce and gives a thumbs-up. Blue handwriting addressed to Joyce runs across the lower left.
A wide grayscale print shows Blackwell's central tower rising above two long wings, with evergreens behind them. The white border names the academy and advertises free campus tours.
Oversized pink and black Halloween Bazaar lettering fills an orange poster. A dark hill with crooked gravestones rises across the bottom, opposite a bare tree.
A Pan Estates advertisement shows a narrow brown house with a steep roof, a front staircase and a garage below. Tall evergreens surround it. A green Prescott Development box overlaps the lawn.
Two woven cord bracelets lie together, their loose ends knotted. The red and blue bracelet carries a silver C charm. The purple, yellow and white one carries an R.
A black-and-white gig flyer places Psychedelic Apocalypse above stacked loudspeakers. Bold lettering, abstract shapes and diagonal stripes fill the remaining space.
A silver recordable CD has Rachel Songs handwritten in blue above the center hole. Black writing near the bottom has been heavily crossed out.
A torn, crumpled sheet of graph paper begins with a lone C. Dense blue handwriting fills the page. Whole lines near the bottom disappear under thick scribbles.
On a stained, creased scrap, four words in jagged dark strokes fill two lines. They read I want to die.
A narrow photo-booth strip shows Chloe and Rachel in three black-and-white poses. They pull faces, laugh with their mouths open, then lean their heads together for the last shot.
A stained Vortex Club flyer turns a gray city building into a block of lettering. Block Party fills one side in orange. The date and DJ name run down the darker side.

A wide forest picture contrasts dark foreground trunks and green undergrowth with pale, misty trees in the distance. A narrow path curves from the lower right toward the center, passing a jagged, moss-covered stump. Tall, straight trunks extend beyond the top of the picture.

A tall, pale lighthouse rises from a dark rocky cliff beside a low building and sparse evergreen trees. Three birds cross the light sky. Muted gray and brown tones and a low viewpoint emphasize the tower's height. Glossy glare washes across the left side of the picture.
Loose pen sketches share a white sheet. A barefoot figure poses beside a stool, hands at the waist. Below are a photographer with a camera to their eye, a broad back and a skull in profile.

Eight young people pose in two rows around classroom tables, five in front and three behind. At front center, a purple-haired person wears a sleeveless gray top and layered necklaces. A bright pink hoodie stands out in the back row. Glossy glare crosses the photograph's right side and the tables below.

The cover of Capturing the Image by Mark Jefferson shows a face partly hidden by a black camera. A blue stripe caps the cover. The title and author's name sit in black bands above and below the portrait.
A blue-ink caricature shows a scowling man with an enormous balding head hunched on a small block. Above him, handwritten words ask, What's your problem?

A glossy magazine cover centers a front-facing woman with long dark hair, a black bra and a long black necklace. Her portrait overlaps tall white title letters against a dark teal background. Yellow and white cover lines flank her head, including Noir Beauty and Film vs Digital. A pale barcode box sits at the lower right.

A black Pop Vine magazine cover uses oversized yellow and pink title lettering and the red-and-green question Is Grunge Dead? A long-haired woman in a black leather jacket and cropped top looks down at a camera held near her waist. Bright blue text strips and small yellow-bordered pictures crowd the lower corners.
A grayscale campus poster centers Blackwell's tower between two long classroom wings. White lettering in the treetops reads Blackwell Academy, Our Past, Your Future.
A thin black rectangle frames a white hall conduct notice. Four short rules sit one below the other in rounded black lettering, each beginning with No.
A navy poster shows four students reaching up around a blue and green globe. Curved white lettering above them reads The World Is Yours Today.

Four overlapping notices mix handwriting and cartoon artwork. A blue handwritten band advertisement with musical doodles fills the left. Above it, a white Bible-study notice has a black cross and tiny heart. At right, a turquoise swimming poster shows an otter in red arm floats; a small yellow tablet-sale note overlaps its lower corner.
A snowman in a red scarf and knit cap stands on a snowy hillside under the headline Global Warning, Freak Snow. A meeting time fills the white space below.

A dark Halloween blood-drive poster centers a white cartoon bat with outstretched wings, oversized ears and bright blue hair. Red drips stain its open mouth and chest. Distressed red lettering at the top reads Blood: Give It Up. White event details and a red prize banner fill the lower portion of the scuffed, glossy sheet.
Thick black handwriting across a creased sheet reads Stop Being a Loser! Below, a blue outline arrow points to a smaller red End of the World Party flyer taped to the sheet.
A gray figure tumbles headfirst into a black spiral beneath the stacked words Enter the Vortex Club. Don't Be Left Out cuts diagonally across the upper corner.
Yellow End of the World Party lettering glows above an orange mushroom cloud. The date sits at the top and Blackwell Swimming Pool appears in the lower right against dark red bands.
Fiery streaks fall toward a curved red horizon on a dark party flyer. A white Vortex Club logo tops the large yellow title. The pool location and Thursday date sit directly underneath.
A dark globe glows red around the edges as fiery objects streak toward it. Yellow End of the World Party lettering fills the sky above, with the pool location in white below.
Two blue pins hold up a creased Front to the Future poster. Cartoon figures in old-fashioned clothes stand beneath the heading, one raising a small flask.
A parchment-colored poster pairs the words Science Is Art and Art Is Science. Between them are fine drawings of a bearded face, a human figure in a circle, a horse and a winged flying machine.
